article.story: TUSCALOOSA, Ala. -- — Austin Mack threw for 254 yards and four touchdowns, leading No. 7 Alabama past Chattanooga 47-0 on Saturday in its final tuneup before the Iron Bowl. Mack made his first collegiate start for the Crimson Tide (9-2, 6-2 SEC, No. 3 CFP) in place of Keelon Russell, who injured his ankle against LSU but played against Vanderbilt last week. Alabama’s NIL collective, Yea Alabama, announced the change before kickoff. Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer said Russell did not aggravate the injury against Vanderbilt and is expected to practice normally next week. “We didn’t want to risk anything with putting him in a vulnerable position,” DeBoer said. “He’s on the homestretch. Looking really good and I’d expect him to be going full speed, full go all week.” Both coaches agreed to shorten the fourth quarter to 10 minutes. Alabama built a 40-0 lead before pulling most of its starters midway through the third quarter. Mack completed 20 of 25 passes before giving way to Jett Thomalla. Mack has played under DeBoer since 2023 at Washington and backed up Jalen Milroe, Ty Simpson and Russell at Alabama. “I wanted to show the world what I was capable of,” Mack said. Mack said he felt nervous early and left the pocket too soon on some plays before settling into a rhythm. He credited his offensive line with helping him operate the offense and his receivers with being where they needed to be. “Once he started, you know, you could see him starting to make his checks and getting in that rhythm and in and out of the huddle,” DeBoer said. DeBoer pointed to Mack’s touchdown pass to Rico Scott at the end of a two-minute drive before halftime as an example of the quarterback settling in and trusting his pass catchers. Daniel Hill and Trae’shawn Brown both eclipsed 70 yards on the ground as the Crimson Tide rushed for 234 yards. The defense held Chattanooga (7-5, 6-3 Southern Conference) to 87 yards. Besides Scott, Ryan Coleman-Williams, Lotzeir Brooks, Noah Rodgers and Kevin Riley also caught touchdown passes while Mack added a rushing score. The Takeaway Chattanooga: The Mocs struggled against Alabama’s trench play and could not sustain drives, finishing their regular season with a shutout loss. Alabama: Beating an FCS opponent is unlikely to boost its AP ranking, but Mack’s performance showed the Tide has a capable backup in case Russell misses any time in the postseason. Up Next Chattanooga: Completed its regular season Saturday.
